title: The fall 2025 government shutdown
summary: Government funding lapsed on October 1, 2025 after the Senate could not reach the 60 votes needed to advance either a Republican-backed continuing resolution (H.R. 5371) or a Democratic alternative (S. 2882), which also extended expiring health insurance subsidies. The Senate voted on the two bills repeatedly before passing an amended H.R. 5371 on November 10, 2025, 60–40.

summary.text: Continuing Appropriations, Agriculture, Legislative Branch, Military Construction and Veterans Affairs, and Extensions Act, 2026 This act ends the government shutdown that began on October 1, 2025, by providing FY2026 continuing appropriations for most federal agencies through January 30, 2026, and providing appropriations through the end of FY2026 for agriculture, military construction and veterans affairs, and legislative branch programs. It also extends various expiring programs and authorities. (Sec. 3) This section provides that references to this Act included in any division of this act refer only to the provisions of that division unless the act expressly provides otherwise. (Sec. 4) This section provides that the explanatory statement regarding this act that was printed in the Congressional Record has the same effect with respect to the allocation of funds and implementation of Divisions B through D of this act as a joint explanatory statement of a conference committee. (Sec. 5) This section specifies that the sums in this act are appropriated for FY2026. Continuing Appropriations and Extensions and Other Matters Act, 2026 This bill provides continuing FY2026 appropriations for federal agencies, permanently extends the expanded premium tax credit for purchasing health insurance, provides additional funding for Medicaid and security for federal officials, and extends various expiring programs. Specifically, the bill provides continuing FY2026 appropriations to federal agencies through the earlier of October 31, 2025, or the enactment of the applicable appropriations act. It is known as a continuing resolution (CR) and prevents a government shutdown that would otherwise occur if the FY2026 appropriations bills have not been enacted when FY2026 begins on October 1, 2025. The CR funds most programs and activities at the FY2025 levels with several exceptions that provide funding flexibility and additional appropriations for various programs. For example, the CR provides additional funding for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting and security for federal officials. promises.name: Gary C. Peters
promises.quote: I will be voting no on the DHS funding bill because it lacks necessary reforms to immigration enforcement.
promises.promise: Said he will vote no on the DHS funding bill lacking immigration-enforcement reforms.

promises.name: Cory A. Booker
promises.quote:
As I've always said, I will not support a government funding bill that continues to raise our costs, jeopardizes our health care, and hurts the people of my state.

I’m urging my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to stand up for Americans who are counting on us to lower their costs, and address the urgent, and–in too many cases–dire challenges people are facing in our country. 

I will not let up in this fight.

I will vote no.
promises.promise: Said he will vote no on a government funding bill that raises costs and jeopardizes health care.

promises.name: John W. Hickenlooper
promises.quote:
Donald Trump knows the Senate can’t pass a bill to fund the government without 7 Democratic votes. So why is he refusing to negotiate?

I will not be one of those 7 unless we address skyrocketing costs caused by health care cuts and tariffs.
promises.promise: Said he will not vote for a government funding bill unless it addresses health care costs and tariffs.

promises.name: Cory A. Booker
promises.quote:
As I have said, I will not give away my vote to Trump to fund the government for nothing. 

A funding bill that continues to raise our costs, jeopardizes our health care, and hurts the people of my state does not have my support.
promises.promise: Said he will not support a government funding bill that raises costs and jeopardizes health care.

statements.name: Shelley Moore Capito
statements.quote: I urge my colleagues to end this shutdown, restore stability, and put the safety of our Nation first.

statements.name: Gary C. Peters
statements.quote: I voted no on the funding bill today because we need serious reforms to require @DHSgov immigration enforcement operations to be conducted safely and responsibly. I urge our Republican colleagues to let us vote to fund the rest of the government and work with us to rein in DHS.

statements.name: Roger Marshall
statements.quote: I will tell the Presiding Officer: No one wins when there is a government shutdown--especially when it goes on this long--and it is certainly not the American people.

statements.name: Dan Sullivan
statements.quote: As Senator Johnson just said, have a little bit of conscience and a little bit of courage, the kind of courage that our military displays every day, and vote for the Shutdown Fairness Act right now.

statements.name: Gary C. Peters
statements.quote: I will continue to work to this end and to work to end this government shutdown and address the healthcare crisis, but in the meantime, we must protect our hard-working Federal employees.

statements.name: James E. Risch
statements.quote: The Democrat shutdown has limited services on our public lands, stifling access to our great outdoors. I will continue to put Idaho and our public lands first, and vote for the clean funding bill that will reopen our government.

statements.name: Lisa Murkowski
statements.quote: We need to act to end this shutdown, and I am going to call on all of my colleagues to stay here until we get it done.

statements.name: Pete Ricketts
statements.quote: My offices across the state remain open.  My team remains available to help Nebraskans.  I will keep fighting to end this Schumer Shutdown and restore essential services.

statements.name: Katie Boyd Britt
statements.quote: First, passing the CR, of course, will avert a harmful and unnecessary government shutdown.

statements.name: Tina Smith
statements.quote: Trump and Republicans are making your life more expensive. I voted against his funding bill because it doesn’t come close to meeting the needs of Minnesotans.  Many of the projects it cut have to happen regardless, and without federal support, you’ll be the one paying for it.
